  "evidence_ids": [

  ],
  "reasons": [
    "Capital receipts are those receipts that either create a liability (such as borrowings/loans) or reduce financial assets (such as disinvestment/sale of PSU shares).",
    "Here, loans of Rs 800 crore create a liability and PSU share sales of Rs 300 crore reduce financial assets, making total capital receipts Rs 800 crore + Rs 300 crore = Rs 1,100 crore.",
    "The Rs 600 crore of other receipts neither create a liability nor reduce financial assets, classifying them as revenue receipts rather than capital receipts."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Government Budget & the Economy",
  "syllabus_topic": "Classification of receipts - revenue receipts and capital receipts",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "Receipts creating a liability or reducing financial assets are classified as capital receipts.",
      "status": "convention",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": [
        "E1.1",
        "E1.2"
      ]
    },
    {
      "condition": "Loans of Rs 800 crore, disinvestment of Rs 300 crore, and other receipts of Rs 600 crore were received during the year.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "B",
      "strongest_reading": "Only debt-creating receipts like loans are counted as capital receipts, excluding asset sales.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "All receipts of the government regardless of whether they create liability or reduce assets are summed.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "Only non-debt capital receipts arising from the sale of PSU shares are counted.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",

    }
  ],

  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "arithmetic",
      "evidence_id": "",
      "premise_quote": "Rs 800 crore as loans from agencies to which they must be returned, Rs 300 crore from the sale of its shares in Public Sector Undertakings",
      "reason": "800 + 300 = Rs 1,100 crore, as both components satisfy the capital receipt definition."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",

      "premise_source": "arithmetic",

      "reason": "Omits the Rs 300 crore PSU disinvestment which reduces financial assets."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",

      "premise_source": "arithmetic",

      "reason": "Erroneously includes Rs 600 crore of revenue receipts in capital receipts."
    },
    {

      "reason": "Omits Rs 800 crore of borrowings which create a liability."
    }
  ]
